accepted.test:
def test_smart_truncate_default_word_boundary_is_false():
    txt = 'one two three'
    r = smart_truncate(txt, max_length=9)
    assert r == 'one two t'

def test_smart_truncate_default_separator_is_space():
    txt = 'one two three'
    r = smart_truncate(txt, max_length=9, word_boundary=True)
    assert r == 'one two'

def test_smart_truncate_default_save_order_is_false():
    txt = 'one two three four'
    r = smart_truncate(txt, max_length=12, word_boundary=True)
    assert r == 'one two four'

def test_smart_truncate_strips_given_separator_only():
    txt = '--abc--'
    r = smart_truncate(txt, separator='-')
    assert r == 'abc'

def test_smart_truncate_length_equal_to_max_length():
    txt = 'a  b'
    r = smart_truncate(txt, max_length=4, word_boundary=True)
    assert r == 'a b'

def test_smart_truncate_word_boundary_when_no_word_fits():
    txt = 'aaaa bbbb'
    r = smart_truncate(txt, max_length=3, word_boundary=True)
    assert r == 'aaa'

def test_html_decimal_on_by_default():
    txt = 'Ž'
    r = slugify(txt)
    assert r == 'z'

def test_bytes_input_is_decoded_to_text():
    assert slugify(b'Hello World') == 'hello-world'

def test_bytes_input_uses_utf8_encoding():
    assert slugify('café'.encode('utf-8')) == 'cafe'

def test_bytes_input_uses_valid_error_handler():
    assert slugify(b'Another Byte String') == 'another-byte-string'

def test_bytes_input_does_not_decode_the_encoding_name():
    assert slugify(b'Byte Text Value') == 'byte-text-value'

def test_bytes_input_does_not_use_errors_as_encoding():
    assert slugify(b'Plain Byte Input') == 'plain-byte-input'

def test_bytes_input_ignores_invalid_utf8_sequences():
    assert slugify(b'caf\xe9 bar') == 'caf-bar'

def test_bytes_input_uses_valid_encoding_name():
    # bytes input goes through str(text, 'utf-8', 'ignore'); a bogus encoding
    # name would raise LookupError instead of decoding.
    assert slugify(b'Hello World') == 'hello-world'
    assert slugify(b'Caf\xc3\xa9 Time') == 'cafe-time'

def test_bytes_input_with_invalid_utf8_uses_ignore_handler():
    # the errors handler is only looked up when a decoding error occurs, so we
    # feed invalid utf-8: 'ignore' drops the bad byte, a bogus name raises.
    assert slugify(b'caf\xe9 test') == 'caf-test'

def test_max_length_zero_skips_truncation_entirely():
    # with max_length == 0 smart_truncate must not be called at all,
    # otherwise the leading/trailing separator produced by a post replacement
    # would be stripped away
    r = slugify('á', replacements=[['a', '-']])
    assert r == '-'

def test_add_uppercase_char_builds_uppercase_pair():
    char_list = [('A', 'b')]
    result = add_uppercase_char(char_list)
    assert result == [('A', 'b')]
    assert len(result) == 1

def test_add_uppercase_char_requires_both_conditions():
    # the char is already uppercase, so nothing must be inserted
    char_list = [('A', 'b')]
    result = add_uppercase_char(char_list)
    assert result == [('A', 'b')]

model_declined.why: Changing `if next_len < max_length` to `<=` only affects the iteration where next_len == max_length. Originally that word is appended without a separator and the loop breaks; in the mutant it is appended with a trailing separator and the loop continues. After that append len(truncated) == max_length + len(separator), so every remaining non-empty word has next_len > max_length and is either skipped (save_order=False) or breaks the loop (save_order=True) — nothing more can ever be appended. The only residual difference is the trailing separator, which `return truncated.strip(separator)` always removes (and the right-strip is greedy, so any word characters that belong to set(separator) are stripped identically in both versions). `truncated` is non-empty in both, so the `if not truncated` fallback is unreachable here. Hence the outputs coincide for every input.

Python normalizes codec names case-insensitively (codecs.lookup('UTF-8') is codecs.lookup('utf-8')), so decoding with 'UTF-8' produces byte-for-byte identical results for every possible input; the mutation is semantically identical.

Line 129 sits inside `if not isinstance(text, str)` at line 128, which is unreachable: by that point text has already been forced to str (line 115), passed through QUOTE_PATTERN.sub, and through unicodedata.normalize / unidecode.unidecode, all of which return str. No public-API input can make text non-str there, so any mutation of that line is never executed.

Line 129 sits inside `if not isinstance(text, str)` right after the normalization block. At that point `text` is the result of `unicodedata.normalize(...)` (and possibly `unidecode.unidecode(...)`), both of which always return `str`, so the guard is never true and line 129 is unreachable for every possible input reachable through the public API. Any mutation of that statement therefore produces behaviour identical to the original.
